---
title: "Predictive model"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
df-print: kable
---

Purpose: across species, is the subadult - adult contrast phylogenetically structured, or related
to habitat breadth, aquatic habit or an extended larval period (Q7)? Replaces
`size_bd_unified/05_species_regression.qmd` (built on m11g, retired 2026-11-25). Specification
and reasons: `README.md` "Downstream models" -> "Predictive model".

In short:

- **response**: each species' mean contrast from stage 1 (prevalence and load in one
  multivariate model, so their phylogenetic correlation is estimated), with its posterior sd as
  a known standard error. Tier D species get an inflated se (`03`).
- **predictors**: log habitat breadth and aquatic index (standardized), extended larval period
  (age at metamorphosis > 12 months, overwintering larvae; 8 of 31 species), and a phylogenetic
  random effect.
- **fits**:
  - *main*: stage 1 mean contrasts, all species (31 prevalence, 30 load)
  - *same-condition* (sensitivity): species contrasts from co-sampled events only (`04`; 22 /
    15 species). Every species then contributes the same kind of contrast (README "How to read
    the results", "As-sampled contrasts")
  - *check*: main + the share of swabs in co-sampled events (that part's definition). Its slope
    near 0 = the same-condition / realized mix does not shift contrasts systematically
  - *ordinal* (sensitivity): age at metamorphosis as an ordered predictor (D < R < M < E) with a
    monotonic effect; only its total effect is readable (D and R hold 1 and 2 species)

Reading: posterior medians with 50 / 95% intervals and pd. With 31 species, slopes will be
uncertain; a wide interval centered near 0 means "not informed", not "no effect".

Run order: `01_contrast_tiers.Rmd`, `03_contrast_analysis.Rmd` (writes
`03_predictive_responses.csv`), `04_contrast_environment_screen.qmd` (writes
`04_same_condition_species_contrasts.csv`), then this script. Fits are small (seconds to minutes)
and cached with `file =`.

# Setup
```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, cmdstanr, posterior, tidybayes, ape, priorsense)

intermediates_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "intermediates")
models_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "models", "predictive")
dir.create(models_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# conv_check() (shared with the other brms analyses)
source(here("size_bd_season", "season_check_functions.R"))

set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))

```

# Data
```{r}
# responses: one row per species x part
#   stage 1 (03): contrast_mean, contrast_sd, contrast_se (tier D inflated), tier,
#                 pct_swabs_co_event (share of swabs in co-sampled events, part definition)
#   same-condition (04): contrast_mean, contrast_sd from co-sampled events only
responses_main = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "03_predictive_responses.csv"),
                          show_col_types = FALSE)
responses_sc = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "04_same_condition_species_contrasts.csv"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE)

# traits. habitat breadth and aquatic index: IUCN habitat metrics (as in the unified 05).
# age at metamorphosis: species notes (D direct, R < 2 months, M 2-12 months, E > 12 months;
# codings for r. catesbeiana, r. clamitans and h. phyllodes fixed 2026-11-26). the first data row
# of the notes file holds the code legend, so rows without a species are dropped
habitat = read_csv(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "iucn_habitat_metrics.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, habitat_breadth, aquatic_index)

species_notes = read_csv(here("data", "species_notes_2026-11-26.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE,
                         name_repair = "unique_quiet") %>%
  filter(!is.na(species)) %>%
  transmute(taxon_capture = species, age_metamorphosis = `Age at Metamorphosis`)

traits = habitat %>%
  inner_join(species_notes, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% responses_main$taxon_capture)

# every species with a response needs traits (expected: none missing)
setdiff(unique(responses_main$taxon_capture), traits$taxon_capture)

# predictors, scaled once over the main species set (reused in every fit):
#   log_hb_z         log habitat breadth, standardized (per sd)
#   aquatic_z        aquatic index, standardized (per sd)
#   extended_larval  +0.5 extended larval period (E), -0.5 otherwise: the slope is the difference
#                    between the two groups, the intercept their midpoint (as stage_c in stage 1)
#   age_met_ord      ordered factor D < R < M < E for the monotonic variant
traits = traits %>%
  mutate(log_hb_z = as.numeric(scale(log(habitat_breadth))),
         aquatic_z = as.numeric(scale(aquatic_index)),
         extended_larval = if_else(age_metamorphosis == "E", 0.5, -0.5),
         age_met_ord = factor(age_metamorphosis, levels = c("D", "R", "M", "E"), ordered = TRUE))

traits %>% count(age_metamorphosis)

# predictor correlations (31 species): high values make separate slopes uncertain
round(cor(traits %>% transmute(log_hb_z, aquatic_z, extended_larval)), 2)

# phylogenetic correlation matrix (diag = 1, so the phylogenetic sd is on the same scale as
# sigma and their ratio reads as a phylogenetic signal), pruned to the species modeled
phylo_tree = read.tree(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "phylo_tree.nwk"))
setdiff(traits$taxon_capture, phylo_tree$tip.label)   # expected: none
phylo_tree = keep.tip(phylo_tree, traits$taxon_capture)
A = vcv.phylo(phylo_tree, corr = TRUE)

# wide data for the multivariate model: one row per species, one response column per part.
# a part a species lacks (e.g. b. faber load) is excluded with subset(); its response and se are
# filled with placeholders (0, 1) so brms does not drop the whole row
make_wide = function(responses, se_col) {
  responses %>%
    transmute(taxon_capture, part, y = contrast_mean, se = .data[[se_col]],
              share_z = if ("pct_swabs_co_event" %in% names(responses)) pct_swabs_co_event else NA_real_) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = c(y, se, share_z), names_glue = "{part}_{.value}") %>%
    rename(prevalence = prevalence_y, load = load_y) %>%
    mutate(has_prevalence = !is.na(prevalence), has_load = !is.na(load),
           across(c(prevalence, load), ~ coalesce(.x, 0)),
           across(c(prevalence_se, load_se), ~ coalesce(.x, 1))) %>%
    left_join(traits, by = "taxon_capture")
}

data_main = make_wide(responses_main, "contrast_se") %>%
  # check-fit predictor: share of swabs in co-sampled events, standardized within each part
  mutate(prevalence_share_z = as.numeric(scale(prevalence_share_z)),
         load_share_z = if_else(has_load, as.numeric(scale(if_else(has_load, load_share_z, NA_real_))), 0))
data_sc = make_wide(responses_sc, "contrast_sd")

data_main %>% summarise(n_species = n(), n_prevalence = sum(has_prevalence), n_load = sum(has_load))
data_sc %>% summarise(n_species = n(), n_prevalence = sum(has_prevalence), n_load = sum(has_load))

```

# Model
```{r}
# one formula per part:
#   y | se(se, sigma = TRUE)   y ~ N(mu, sqrt(sigma^2 + se^2)): se = the species' known
#                              estimation error; sigma = species variation beyond it that is not
#                              phylogenetic
#   + subset(has_*)            species without that part are left out of it
#   (1 | p | gr(taxon_capture, cov = A))
#                              phylogenetic effect (species correlated by shared ancestry); the
#                              shared "p" estimates the correlation between the prevalence and
#                              load effects
# rescor = FALSE: no residual correlation (not identifiable with known se)
predictive_bf = function(part, rhs) {
  bf(as.formula(paste0(part, " | se(", part, "_se, sigma = TRUE) + subset(has_", part, ") ~ ",
                       rhs, " + (1 | p | gr(taxon_capture, cov = A))")))
}

rhs_main = "1 + log_hb_z + aquatic_z + extended_larval"
rhs_ord = "1 + log_hb_z + aquatic_z + mo(age_met_ord)"

formula_main = mvbf(predictive_bf("prevalence", rhs_main), predictive_bf("load", rhs_main), rescor = FALSE)
formula_check = mvbf(predictive_bf("prevalence", paste(rhs_main, "+ prevalence_share_z")),
                     predictive_bf("load", paste(rhs_main, "+ load_share_z")), rescor = FALSE)
formula_ord = mvbf(predictive_bf("prevalence", rhs_ord), predictive_bf("load", rhs_ord), rescor = FALSE)

# priors, on the contrast scale (prevalence: logit; load: log load among positives):
#   intercepts normal(0, 2) / normal(0, 3), as the stage 1 mean contrasts
#   slopes normal(0, 1): a one-sd change in a trait (or extended vs not) shifting the mean
#     contrast by more than ~2 units is implausible
#   phylogenetic sd and sigma exponential(1); correlation lkj(2)
# the monotonic variant's step proportions keep brms' default dirichlet(1)
predictive_priors = c(
  set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept", resp = "prevalence"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 3)", class = "Intercept", resp = "load"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", resp = "prevalence"),
  set_prior("normal(0, 1)", class = "b", resp = "load"),
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd", resp = "prevalence"),
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd", resp = "load"),
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sigma", resp = "prevalence"),
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sigma", resp = "load"),
  set_prior("lkj(2)", class = "cor"))

fit_predictive = function(formula, data, name) {
  brm(formula, data = data, data2 = list(A = A[data$taxon_capture, data$taxon_capture]),
      family = gaussian(), prior = predictive_priors,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
      chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 128, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
      file = file.path(models_dir, name), file_refit = "on_change")
}

predictive_fits = list(
  main           = fit_predictive(formula_main,  data_main, "predictive_main"),
  same_condition = fit_predictive(formula_main,  data_sc,   "predictive_same_condition"),
  check          = fit_predictive(formula_check, data_main, "predictive_check"),
  ordinal        = fit_predictive(formula_ord,   data_main, "predictive_ordinal"))

# sampler checks (thresholds in conv_check)
map_dfr(predictive_fits, conv_check, .id = "fit")

```

# Checks
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10

# posterior predictive check per part (main fit): the spread of species contrasts the model
# expects vs the observed means
map(c("prevalence", "load"), ~ pp_check(predictive_fits$main, resp = .x, ndraws = 100) +
      ggtitle(.x))

# prior sensitivity (power-scaling; small model, so the full check is cheap): "prior" > 0.05 on
# a slope = it follows its prior more than the data (expected for weakly informed traits)
ps_vars = grep("^(b|sd|sigma)_", variables(predictive_fits$main), value = TRUE)
powerscale_sensitivity(predictive_fits$main, variable = ps_vars) %>%
  filter(diagnosis != "-")

```

# Results
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 11

# trait slopes per fit: change in the mean contrast per sd of the trait (log habitat breadth,
# aquatic index, co-sampling share), or between extended and other larval periods. median,
# 50 / 95% intervals, pd
slope_draws = imap_dfr(predictive_fits, function(fit, name) {
  as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^(b|bsp)_(prevalence|load)_", regex = TRUE) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    select(starts_with("b"), -contains("Intercept")) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(fit = name,
           part = str_match(parameter, "_(prevalence|load)_")[, 2],
           term = sub("^(b|bsp)_(prevalence|load)_", "", parameter))
})

(slope_summary = slope_draws %>%
  group_by(fit, part, term) %>%
  summarise(median = median(value),
            lower_50 = quantile(value, 0.25), upper_50 = quantile(value, 0.75),
            lower_95 = quantile(value, 0.025), upper_95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
            pd = max(mean(value > 0), mean(value < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  arrange(part, term, fit))

# main vs same-condition vs check, the shared terms: agreement = trait conclusions do not rest on
# the same-condition / realized mix
slope_draws %>%
  filter(fit %in% c("main", "same_condition", "check"),
         term %in% c("log_hb_z", "aquatic_z", "extended_larval")) %>%
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("check", "same_condition", "main"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = term, color = fit)) +
  stat_pointinterval(.width = c(0.5, 0.95), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ part, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = labeller(part = c(prevalence = "prevalence (logit)", load = "load among positives (log)"))) +
  labs(x = "change in the mean contrast (median, 50 / 95%)", y = NULL, color = "fit",
       subtitle = "per sd of log habitat breadth / aquatic index; extended_larval = extended - other") +
  theme_classic()

```

## Phylogenetic signal and the prevalence - load correlation
```{r}
# phylogenetic signal per part: sd_phylo^2 / (sd_phylo^2 + sigma^2), the share of species
# variation beyond estimation error that follows the phylogeny (reads like Pagel's lambda, since
# A is a correlation matrix). with ~31 species the two sds are only partly separable, so expect
# wide intervals. cor_p = correlation of the phylogenetic effects on the prevalence and load
# contrasts
signal_summary = imap_dfr(predictive_fits[c("main", "same_condition")], function(fit, name) {
  dr = as_draws_df(fit) %>% as_tibble()
  tibble(.draw = dr$.draw,
         h2_prevalence = dr$sd_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept^2 /
           (dr$sd_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept^2 + dr$sigma_prevalence^2),
         h2_load = dr$sd_taxon_capture__load_Intercept^2 /
           (dr$sd_taxon_capture__load_Intercept^2 + dr$sigma_load^2),
         cor_prevalence_load = dr$cor_taxon_capture__prevalence_Intercept__load_Intercept) %>%
    pivot_longer(-.draw, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(fit = name)
}) %>%
  group_by(fit, metric) %>%
  summarise(median = median(value),
            lower_50 = quantile(value, 0.25), upper_50 = quantile(value, 0.75),
            lower_95 = quantile(value, 0.025), upper_95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
            pd = max(mean(value > 0), mean(value < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))

signal_summary

```

# Export
```{r}
write_csv(slope_summary, file.path(intermediates_dir, "05_predictive_slopes.csv"))
write_csv(signal_summary, file.path(intermediates_dir, "05_predictive_signal.csv"))
```
